mechanism_narrative: The four-week upward slope in TRANSIT from -30.9 to -24.7 signals commuter activity returning; each further weekly gain above -25 lifts retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will exceed its last-28-day mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is less than or equal to its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A fall in TRANSIT below -30 for two consecutive weeks indicates renewed policy-driven movement restrictions that suppress discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days will be lower than its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses below -30 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-14-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean after TRANSIT prints below -30 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rises toward baseline while RESIDENTIAL falls from its elevated level, workers shift from home to out-of-home routines; this interaction raises RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -12 and RESIDENTIAL falls below 12
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-14-day mean is lower than its last-28-day mean when WORKPLACES > -12 and RESIDENTIAL < 12.

mechanism_narrative: In the early-March seasonal window, a PARKS rebound above -10 signals favorable outdoor conditions that spill over into retail-and-recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days will be higher than its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10 for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-7-day mean is lower than its last-28-day mean when PARKS is above -10.

mechanism_narrative: A RESIDENTIAL reading above 10 means households remain confined at home, reducing shopping-center and restaurant trips; RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will stay below its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week, the joint signal indicates tighter movement policy; the interaction suppresses retail trips, so RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days will be lower than its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall by at least 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-14-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean after TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall by at least 1 point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM recovery from -7.1 to -4.3 signals normalized essential errands that also lift adjacent retail footfall; RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will exceed its last-28-day mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: In a pre-lockdown regime, a widening gap between falling TRANSIT and rising RESIDENTIAL indicates voluntary avoidance that precedes retail decline; RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days will be lower than its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls while RESIDENTIAL rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-14-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean when TRANSIT falls while RESIDENTIAL rises for two consecutive weeks.
